mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.5% over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 2.5% fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 5.0% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates broad demand contraction that lowers corporate revenue expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO > 120) signals easing supply constraints and expanding manufacturing output, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) when INDPRO exceeds 120 over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200,000 jobs per month signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 200,000 jobs in prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS growth exceeds 200,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 3.0% for three months indicates accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 3.0% for three months fails to produce positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 50% of cases over the last 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI increase above 2.5% signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 115 for two consecutive months indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO falls below 115 for two months.
